passages.text: When your house is on fire, you rescue the pot that’s useful, not the one that’s burnt. And as the world is on fire with old age and death, you should rescue by giving, for what’s given is rescued. What’s given has happiness as its fruit, but not what isn’t given. Bandits take it, or rulers, it’s consumed by fire, or lost. Then in the end this corpse is cast off, along with all your possessions. Knowing this, an intelligent person would enjoy what they have and also give it away.
passages.note: Possessions don't last; enjoying and sharing what you have

passages.text: What’s still good in old age? What’s good when grounded? What is people’s treasure? What’s hard for thieves to take? Ethics are still good in old age. Faith is good when grounded. Wisdom is people’s treasure. Merit’s hard for thieves to take.
passages.note: Ageing; what keeps its value over a lifetime

passages.text: Who’s your friend while journeying? Who’s your friend at home? Who’s your friend in time of need? Who’s your friend in lives to come? A caravan is your friend while journeying. Mother is your friend at home. An ally in time of need is a friend time and again. But the good deeds you’ve done yourself—that’s your friend in lives to come.
passages.note: Friendship, support, and the lasting value of good deeds
